title: Reading the next joins from scalar bond distances
claim: Every finite pure-parity presentation reachable by the legal serial rule is recoverable on its current bits from the pairwise scalar bond distances through five. This determines every legal next serial addition and the feasible parallel groups and loose-bit allocations when the policy is evaluated afresh.
standard_statement: Recover the ordinary incidence of finite parity presentations from the minimum size of a bond containing each edge pair. Compare distance-table isometries and actual parent groups under the known rule.
prior_work: The predecessor constructs the orthant from incidence. Its referee recovers the pure finite graph with the full cycle space. The earlier DISTANCE-INFO collision rules out a universal inverse across laws. The first two canonical rounds were piloted before this study.
completion_gate: A reproducible same-size rearrangement test and an all-round theorem or an explicit table collision with different next joins. State the domain precisely.

validation.status: Proved, with separate within-task proof review and two independent finite checks. Automatic finite replays agreed byte for byte.
validation.independence: The census inputs used the entire dual row space, the second check used projections of explicit allowed states and knotlab on fixed examples. A separate analytical reviewer examined the written proof. No external referee verdict for this theorem.

source_contribution: The ordinary pure parity rule and simultaneous policy are declared, including distinct parents, three fresh bits and common-neighbor eligibility. The reader receives only the anonymous scalar table; hidden incidence is used only to grade it.
attained_result: A uniform equivariant inverse on all finite legal histories, including complete cubic rounds. No table-preserving bijection can change the set of permissible next joins. Tested on all 552 presentations through seven junctions; the four-threshold reader passed all and the earlier two-threshold pilot failed on 280.
